body.x: The Confederation and the confederated States foster cohesion between the constituent peoples, the communities and the States (Article 2).

Confederal cohesion rests on the will to live together and on the shared experience of common action. It does not seek to merge the constituent peoples into one: belonging to the Confederation is civic (Article 37); it is added to belonging to a people or to a community, without replacing it.
There is no national register of a Balkan or confederal belonging: the only national registers are those of the seven constituent peoples (Article 102).

Military service and alternative civilian service (Article 60), the national teams and the confederal league (Article 73 bis), the Transbalkanska (Article 95 bis), confederal radio and television (Article 96 bis) and voting days (Article 124 bis) also contribute to confederal cohesion.
Political parties contribute to forming the opinion and the will of citizens.

A confederal party is a party which, at the general election of the Kongres, presents lists in at least twelve constituencies of territorial States belonging to at least three different constituent peoples (Articles 1 bis and 103).

Only confederal parties receive confederal public funding for parties and the airtime that confederal radio and television allocates for the election of the Kongres. The Confederal Chancellery establishes whether a party is a confederal party.
Parties that represent one of the communities of the Council of Communities (Article 1 octies) receive their own public funding and airtime, as set by law.
This Article does not apply to the election of the Narodni Sabor (Article 108).

Every pupil in upper secondary education, general or vocational, spends one semester of his schooling in a territorial State belonging to a constituent people other than that of the State in which he is schooled. A pupil schooled in a confederal territory or in a confederal autonomous municipality freely chooses the host State.
The host State schools the pupil on the same terms as its own pupils.
The Confederation bears the costs of travel and accommodation. It sets the principles of the programme with the States, within the Balkan Education Area (Article 63).
The law governs exemptions and the situation of pupils of schools that teach in the language of an autonomous community.
The curricula of compulsory education include a common core of history of the Confederation, of its peoples and of its communities, which the Confederation sets with the States.

The common core presents the history of each constituent people and of each community, and their relations. It sets out the wars between the peoples without concealing their crimes or imputing collective guilt to any people.
The States freely supplement the common core.
The law setting the common core is subject to the consent of the Narodni Sabor (Article 109 a).
The Confederation honours, in the confederal pantheon, persons whose life or work crossed the borders between the peoples and between the States.
The tribute of the Confederation does not alter the belonging that the person honoured declared or that history recognises; it does not make that person the common property of several peoples.
The law draws up the list of persons honoured and sets the seat of the pantheon. It is subject to the consent of the Narodni Sabor (Article 109 a).

The Day of the Confederation (Dan Konfederacije) is the anniversary of the acceptance of this Constitution by the people and the States (Article 151). It is a public holiday throughout the Confederation.
No confederal public holiday commemorates a battle.
The States set their own public holidays.
